name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage
summary: The lower half of Eagle, the first crewed vehicle to land on the Moon. It stayed behind as a launch pad when the astronauts flew home in the top half.

sources.label: NASA NSSDCA: Apollo 11 Lunar Module (challenge resource)
NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge: Resources (descent stages left behind as launch pads)

site.note: Apollo 11 science package, about 17 m from the lander

name: Apollo 12 ALSEP
summary: A set of science instruments the Apollo 12 astronauts left on the Moon, including a seismometer to feel moonquakes. Earth controlled it until all ALSEP stations were shut down on 30 September 1977.

sources.label: NASA NSSDCA: Apollo 12 Lunar Module / ALSEP (challenge resource)

name: Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo 15
summary: An electric moon buggy that the Apollo 15 astronauts drove to explore up to 5 kilometres from their lander. It is parked on the Moon for good.

sources.label: NASA NSSDCA: Apollo 15 Lunar Module / ALSEP (challenge resource)

name: Surveyor 3
summary: A robot that landed on the Moon in 1967, bouncing twice first. It dug trenches and showed that the ground could hold a lunar module. Two years later, Apollo 12 astronauts walked over and visited it.
